```{r}
# =====================================================================
# Setting up UHC
# =====================================================================

#Load folders of rds batch files 
etosha_dir <- here("data", "batch_output_etosha_XXXX")
west_dir <- here ("data", "batch_output_west_XXX")

#covariates in SSF 
base_terms <- c("core_dist", "fence_dist", "road_dist",
                "water_rivers_dist", "cropland_dist", "grassland",
                "shrubland", "urban_dist", "tree_cover", "elevation",
                "slope", "aspect", "evi", "world_pop")

# extra_vars are covariates kept in the test data but NOT in the model. THey are plotted anyway. 
model_specs <- list(
  etosha_wet = list(pop = "etosha", season = "wet", terms = base_terms, extra_vars = character(0)),
  etosha_dry = list(pop = "etosha", season = "dry", terms = base_terms, extra_vars = character(0)),
  west_wet   = list(pop = "west",   season = "wet", terms = base_terms, extra_vars = character(0)),
  west_dry   = list(pop = "west",   season = "dry", terms = base_terms, extra_vars = character(0))
  # Example: Etosha without core_dist, but still checking whether core_dist
  # is needed by plotting it as an extra variable:
  # etosha_wet_nocore = list(pop = "etosha", season = "wet",
  #                          terms = setdiff(base_terms, "core_dist"),
  #                          extra_vars = "core_dist")
)

prop_train <- 0.8 #80% training / 20% test
split_by <- "id" #instead of splitting random steps, we are splitting elephants, which is stricter than steps
n_samp <- 200 #number of bootstrap draws (grey lines). Should actually be around 1000

max_test_strata <- 20000 #cap on number of test strata used 
seed <- 123 #makes exact same random split and bootstrap draws 

uhc_dir <- here("validation_output", "uhc")
dir.create(uhc_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#Load batches
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------

#Step 1: generate control steps and attach covariates which was already done in SSF. 

#reload finished products 
load_batches <- function(dir) {
  files <- list.files(dir, pattern = "pipeline_batch_.*\\.rds", full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(files) == 0) stop("No pipeline_batch_*.rds files in: ", dir)
  message("Reading ", length(files), " batch files from ", basename(dir))
  
  # Stack all batch files back into one table
  dat <- map_dfr(files, readRDS) |> as_tibble()
  
  #just making sure step_id is there 
   if (!"step_id_" %in% names(dat))
    stop("No 'step_id_' column. Columns: ", paste(names(dat), collapse = ", "))
  
  #Taking elephant idenfier colum (id) an dthe current local step id column (step_id) and brings them together to make unique stratum IDs to prevent data from different elephants leaking into the same group
   dat |> mutate(step_id_ = paste(id, step_id_, sep = "_"))
   
}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------- 
# add transform 
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Not in the workflow: a hook for transformed covariates (sin/cos of aspect, log of population, etc.). It currently does nothing. If there is a transformed variable here, use it in BOTH the SSF and the UHC so the two stay in sync.
# right now there are only raw variables in the model. If we see in the plots that the black falls outside the envelope for aspect, world_pop, or distance variable, that is a problem. 
add_transforms <- function(dat) {
  dat |> mutate(
    # aspect_sin    = sin(aspect * pi / 180),   # uncomment if aspect is in degrees
    # aspect_cos    = cos(aspect * pi / 180),
    # log_world_pop = log1p(world_pop)
  )
}
```

```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# clean_for_uhc()
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#STEP 1 (end): the vignette finishes data prep with
clean_for_uhc <- function(dat, vars) {
  # compares list of covariates the model needs (vars) against columns present in the dataframe. Makes sure no varibles are missing. 
  missing_vars <- setdiff(vars, names(dat))
  if (length(missing_vars) > 0)
    stop("Covariates not in data: ", paste(missing_vars, collapse = ", "))

  dat <- dat |>
    # Looks at the categorical land cover layers, so if a GPS point falls on a pixel where these values are NA, it changes it to 0, so it doesn't drop those rows completely and that it still matches the model. 
    mutate(across(any_of(c("grassland", "shrubland", "tree_cover")), ~ replace_na(.x, 0))) |>
    # Scans every row of the dataset across model variables, so if a row contains NA, the row is dropped. Equivalent to the vignette's na.omit().
    filter(if_all(all_of(vars), is.finite))

  #Groups data by stratum (step_id) and counts the number of case observations and number of available observations. 
  good <- dat |>
    group_by(step_id_) |>
    summarise(n_used = sum(case_), n_avail = sum(!case_), .groups = "drop") |>
    filter(n_used == 1, n_avail >= 1) #Filters list to only strata that meet that case. 

  semi_join(dat, good, by = "step_id_")   # keep only the intact strata
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# split_train_test()
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: split into training and testing datasets.
#We are splitting because we want to see if the test set can be compared agains the model. 
#The demonstration code splits by steps$train <- rbinom(nrow(steps), 1, 0.8)
#Here we split by whole stratum instead of row because the data is grouped (80%) into strata(step_id), where 1 used step is compared against available steps. 
#With by = id, we are holding out entire elephants to know if model can generalize to the broader population

split_train_test <- function(dat, prop_train, by, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)                                    # reproducible split
  units <- if (by == "step") unique(dat$step_id_) else unique(dat$id) #
  train_units <- sample(units, floor(prop_train * length(units)))   # pick ~80% of units
  is_train <- if (by == "step") dat$step_id_ %in% train_units else dat$id %in% train_units
  list(train = dat[is_train, ], test = dat[!is_train, ])
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# subsample_strata()
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#This thins the test set by whole strata to keep the run time manageable since prep_uhc() repeats n_samp
subsample_strata <- function(dat, n_max, seed) {
  if (is.null(n_max)) return(dat)                   # no cap requested
  ids <- unique(dat$step_id_)
  if (length(ids) <= n_max) return(dat)             # already small enough
  set.seed(seed)
  dat |> filter(step_id_ %in% sample(ids, n_max))
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# fit_train_ssf()
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
#STEP 3: use the TRAINING data to fit the candidate model.
fit_train_ssf <- function(train, terms) {
  # Build:  case_ ~ term1 + term2 + ... + strata(step_id_)
  f <- reformulate(c(terms, "strata(step_id_)"), response = "case_")
  fit_clogit(train, f, model = TRUE)
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# run_uhc()
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Runs the whole workflow for ONE model (one population x one season).
run_uhc <- function(pop_dat, spec, model_name) {
  # All columns we need = model terms + extra candidate variables
  all_terms <- unique(c(spec$terms, spec$extra_vars))
  vars      <- unique(all.vars(reformulate(all_terms)))   # underlying column names

  # SAVE TIME: prep_uhc() is slow, so create custom filename label (tag) that includes model name, split, n_samp, and seed.Goes into directory (uhc_dir) to see if file matches existing tag to save time.   
  tag <- paste(model_name, split_by, paste0("n", n_samp), paste0("s", seed), sep = "_")
  out_rds <- file.path(uhc_dir, paste0("uhc_", tag, ".rds"))
  if (file.exists(out_rds)) { message(tag, ": loading saved result"); return(readRDS(out_rds)) }
  message("=== ", tag, " ===")

  #1: data prep 
  # Subset to this model's season, apply transforms, clean.
  # SSF fits wet and dry as separate models, so each gets its own UHC
  dat <- pop_dat |> filter(season == spec$season) |> add_transforms() |> clean_for_uhc(vars)
  message("Rows: ", nrow(dat), " | strata: ", n_distinct(dat$step_id_),
          " | elephants: ", n_distinct(dat$id))
  
   #2: split into train and test 
  sp <- split_train_test(dat, prop_train, split_by, seed)
  message("Train strata: ", n_distinct(sp$train$step_id_),
          " | test strata: ", n_distinct(sp$test$step_id_),
          " | test elephants: ", n_distinct(sp$test$id)) #how many unique strata (step_id_) ended up in train and test, and how many unique animals (id) are in the test set. 

  #Defines list of columns to retain: response (case_), the stratum ID (step_id_) and the covariates same as select(-train)
  #select(-train) deletes that temporary tracking colimn to make the split. 
  #keep_cols keeps the important columns and gets rid of everything else
  keep_cols <- c("case_", "step_id_", vars) 
  train_dat <- sp$train |> select(all_of(keep_cols))
  test_dat  <- sp$test  |> select(all_of(keep_cols)) |> subsample_strata(max_test_strata, seed) 
  
    #3: fit the candidate model on TRAINING data 
  # The model only gets to learn from the training set.
  # Only spec$terms go into the formula. extra_vars stay in test_dat only.
  m_train <- fit_train_ssf(train_dat, spec$terms)
  print(summary(m_train))
  
    #4: prep_uhc() 
  set.seed(seed)    # the bootstrap is random, so fix it for reproducibility
  #running n_samp iterations
  #draws a new set of coefficients from a multivariate normal distribution based on your model's variance-covariance matrix
  #resamples test strata with replacement (empirical bootstrap), simulating what would happen if there was a difference sample of animals
  #calculates distribution of covariates for simulated choices across all iterations (the grey lines)
  #observed used distribution (black line)
  #available distribution (red line)
  uhc <- prep_uhc(object = m_train, test_dat = test_dat, n_samp = n_samp, verbose = TRUE)
  #saveRDS(uhc, out_rds)
  
  #5: plot 
  #The workflow's plain plot(uhc) draws n_samp grey lines per covariate, which is slow with big n_samp.The workflow itself suggests converting the lines to a confidence envelope:dark grey = 95% of the predicted curves, light grey = 100%.
  env <- conf_envelope(as.data.frame(uhc), levels = c(0.95, 1))
  pdf(file.path(uhc_dir, paste0("uhc_plots_", tag, ".pdf")), width = 7, height = 5)
  plot(env)
  dev.off()

  # Free memory before the next model (these objects are big)
  rm(dat, sp, train_dat, test_dat, m_train); gc()
  uhc
}

```

```{r}
# =====================================================================
# RUN
# =====================================================================
# Loop over populations so each population's big dataset is loaded once,
# used for all of its models, then dropped from memory.
uhc_results <- list()
for (pop in c("etosha", "west")) {
  pop_dat <- load_batches(if (pop == "etosha") etosha_dir else west_dir)
  for (nm in names(model_specs)) {
    if (model_specs[[nm]]$pop != pop) next          # only this population's models
    uhc_results[[nm]] <- run_uhc(pop_dat, model_specs[[nm]], nm)
  }
  rm(pop_dat); gc()
}

# plot(uhc_results$etosha_wet["evi"])
# plot(conf_envelope(as.data.frame(uhc_results$etosha_wet), levels = c(0.95, 1)))
```

#===============================
#Boyce Cross-Validation 
#===============================

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# CONTINUOUS BOYCE INDEX VALIDATION FOR Etosha and Western 
# =============================================================================


#0. Packages
library(tidyverse)
library(survival)   # clogit()
library(modEvA)     # Boyce()
library(here)

set.seed(123)       # fold assignment is random


#1. Load the extracted step data 
# NEW: Etosha now comes from the linear-feature script (hr1, lcmixed, crossings already built).
# West must be rerun through extract_lc_mixed() so it has grassland/shrubland/tree_cover.
etosha_all <- readRDS(here("outputs", "ele_trk_extract_etosha_linecross.rds"))
west_all   <- readRDS(here("outputs", "ele_trk_extract_west.rds"))

# NEW: crossing indicators (same logic as the linear-feature script; harmless to re-run on Etosha)
add_crossings <- function(d) {
  lin_cols <- c("kaza_vet_fences_linear", "roads_linear", "hydrorivers_linear")
  stopifnot(all(lin_cols %in% names(d)))
  d |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(
      across(all_of(lin_cols), ~ if_else(is.infinite(.x) | is.na(.x), 0, .x)),  # -Inf/NA = no feature
      fence_cross = as.integer(kaza_vet_fences_linear > 0),
      road_cross  = as.integer(roads_linear > 0),
      river_cross = as.integer(hydrorivers_linear > 0)
    )
}
etosha_all <- add_crossings(etosha_all)
west_all   <- add_crossings(west_all)


#2. Choose covariates and settings
# NEW: base_vars = everything except core_dist; cross_vars = crossing indicators
base_vars  <- c("fence_dist", "road_dist", "water_rivers_dist",
                "cropland_dist", "grassland", "shrubland", "urban_dist",
                "tree_cover", "elevation", "slope", "aspect", "evi", "world_pop")
cross_vars <- c("fence_cross", "road_cross", "river_cross")

#Etosha dropped core_dist because most Etosha steps are inside the core area.
# NEW: West adds core_dist back via `extra`; the three linear-feature scenarios are built from it
make_scenarios <- function(extra = character(0)) {
  list(
    dist_only       = c(extra, base_vars),                                   # 1. distance-to only
    dist_plus_cross = c(extra, base_vars, cross_vars),                       # 2. distance-to + crossings
    cross_only      = c(extra, setdiff(base_vars, c("fence_dist", "road_dist")), cross_vars)  # 3. crossings replace fence/road distance
  )
}

pops <- list(
  Etosha = list(trk = etosha_all, extra = character(0), fill_lc_na = TRUE),
  West   = list(trk = west_all,   extra = "core_dist",  fill_lc_na = FALSE)
)

k_folds <- 5     #number of CV folds (capped at the number of elephants)
bin_width <- 0.1   #moving-window width, in units of the prediction scale
n_windows <- 100   #number of window positions along the gradient (modEvA `res`)
pred_scale <- "rank"  # "rank" or "lp" -- see section 5 for the decision
n_per_stratum <- 11   # 1 used + 10 random steps

boyce_dir <- here("outputs", "boyce")   # NEW: per-model cache folder
dir.create(boyce_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)


#3.Prepare a season-specific dataset 
prep_data <- function(trk, season_label, vars, fill_lc_na = FALSE) {

  stopifnot(all(vars %in% names(trk)))   # NEW: fails loudly if columns are missing (e.g. West without lcmixed)

  d <- trk |>
    as_tibble() |>                       # drop the amt track class; plain tibble is safer
    filter(season == season_label)

  # In Etosha pipeline set missing binary land cover to 0 (pixels outside the land-cover raster). Keep that here.
  if (fill_lc_na) {
    d <- d |> mutate(across(c(grassland, shrubland, tree_cover), ~ replace_na(.x, 0)))
  }

  d |>
    #The same complete rows must be used to fit and to score, so drop NAs in any model covariate up front.
    # NEW: `vars` is the union across all scenarios so every scenario uses identical rows.
    drop_na(all_of(vars)) |>
    # Dropping rows can orphan a stratum (case removed but controls kept, or
    # vice versa). A stratum needs >= 1 case and >= 1 control to be informative.
    group_by(step_id_) |>
    filter(any(case_), any(!case_)) |>
    ungroup()
}


#4.Assign whole elephants to folds
# NEW: now called once per population x season (outside run_ssf_boyce) so all scenarios share folds
make_folds <- function(data, k) {
  ids <- unique(data$id)
  k   <- min(k, length(ids))             #can't have more folds than animals
  fold_tbl <- tibble(id = sample(ids),   #shuffle animals, then deal into folds
                     fold = rep_len(seq_len(k), length(ids)))
  left_join(data, fold_tbl, by = "id")
}


#Fit the SSF and score new steps
fit_ssf <- function(train, vars) {
  f <- reformulate(c(vars, "strata(step_id_)"), response = "case_")
  # With one used step per stratum, method = "efron" gives the same estimates
  # as clogit's default "exact", but is much faster on millions of rows.
  clogit(f, data = train, method = "efron")
}

# Linear predictor for new data: X %*% beta (log relative selection strength).
score_steps <- function(fit, newdata) {
  b <- coef(fit)
  b <- b[!is.na(b)]
  X <- as.matrix(newdata[, names(b)])
  drop(X %*% b)
}


#6.Cross-validated Boyce for one model
# NEW: `data` already has a fold column; `meta` carries population/season/scenario labels
run_ssf_boyce <- function(data, vars, label, meta) {

  folds <- sort(unique(data$fold))
  oof   <- list()   #out-of-fold predictions, kept for the pooled plot
  res   <- list()   #one row of summary stats per fold

  for (f in folds) {
    message(label, ": fold ", f, " of ", length(folds))

    train <- filter(data, fold != f)
    test  <- filter(data, fold == f)

    fit <- fit_ssf(train, vars)
    test$lp <- score_steps(fit, test)      # log-RSS of every held-out step


    #Scale is "rank": Converts the linear predictor into a uniform percentile rank from 0 to 1. Every window gets a roughly equal number of data points, making the P/E ratio stable across the gradient. Boyce is rank-based anyway (Spearman).
    test$pred <- if (pred_scale == "rank") percent_rank(test$lp) else test$lp

    #`obs` must be numeric 0/1 (1 = used step, 0 = random step).
    #modEvA compares predictions at used steps against predictions across
    #ALL steps, i.e. presence vs "available".
    b <- Boyce(obs = as.numeric(test$case_),
               pred = test$pred,
               n.bins = NA,                # NA = continuous moving window
               bin.width = if (pred_scale == "rank") bin_width else "default",
               res = n_windows,
               method = "spearman",
               rm.dup.classes = FALSE,
               plot = FALSE)

    res[[f]] <- tibble(
      meta,                                # NEW: population / season / scenario
      label = label, fold = f,
      n_elephants = n_distinct(test$id),
      n_used_steps = sum(test$case_),
      boyce = b$B,
      #modEvA flags windows with < 30 points (their P/E ratio is noisy)
      n_small_bins = sum(b$bins$bin.N < 30, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
    oof[[f]] <- test |> select(step_id_, case_, lp, pred, fold)
    rm(train, test, fit); gc()             # NEW: free memory between folds
  }

  oof <- bind_rows(oof)

  #Pooled out-of-fold P/E curve
  # A good model gives a monotonically increasing curve. Pooling predictions across folds gives one curve per model.
  Boyce(obs = as.numeric(oof$case_), pred = oof$pred,
        bin.width = if (pred_scale == "rank") bin_width else "default",
        res = n_windows, plot = TRUE,
        main = paste("Boyce (out-of-fold):", label))

  #Check: within-stratum rank of the used step 
  # Because an SSF compares each used step to ITS OWN random steps, also ask:
  # where does the used step rank among the steps in its stratum?
  # (Fortin et al. 2009-style). If the model works, used steps should land at
  # the high ranks far more often than the 1/n expected by chance.
  # NEW: uncommented, and n_per_stratum replaces the max(table(...)) lookup (slow on millions of rows);
  # complete() fills ranks with zero counts so the correlation is always over 1:11
  strata_check <- oof |>
    group_by(step_id_) |>
    filter(n() == n_per_stratum) |>                # keep complete strata (e.g. 11 steps)
    mutate(rank_in_stratum = rank(lp, ties.method = "random")) #method for ranking steps. So when there are steps of identical score, this tie is shuffles them so that they are equally likely to land at any position in it rather than "first" which ranks whichever step comes first which is always the used which gets ranked lowest everytime then.  
    ungroup() |>
    filter(case_) |>
    count(rank_in_stratum, name = "n_used") |>
    complete(rank_in_stratum = 1:n_per_stratum, fill = list(n_used = 0))

  within_stratum_rho <- cor(strata_check$rank_in_stratum, strata_check$n_used,
                            method = "spearman")

  list(label = label,
       folds = bind_rows(res),
       oof = oof,
       within_stratum_counts = strata_check,
       within_stratum_rho = within_stratum_rho)
}


#7. Run for each population x season 
# NEW: also x scenario; each result is cached so reruns skip finished models
boyce_results <- list()

for (pop in names(pops)) {
  scn      <- make_scenarios(pops[[pop]]$extra)
  all_vars <- unique(unlist(scn))

  for (szn in c("wet", "dry")) {
    d <- prep_data(pops[[pop]]$trk, szn, all_vars, fill_lc_na = pops[[pop]]$fill_lc_na)

    set.seed(123)                      # NEW: same fold assignment for every scenario
    d <- make_folds(d, k_folds)

    for (sc in names(scn)) {
      label <- paste(pop, szn, sc)
      path  <- file.path(boyce_dir, paste0(gsub(" ", "_", label), ".rds"))

      if (file.exists(path)) {
        boyce_results[[label]] <- readRDS(path)
      } else {
        meta <- tibble(population = pop, season = szn, scenario = sc)
        boyce_results[[label]] <- run_ssf_boyce(d, scn[[sc]], label, meta)
        saveRDS(boyce_results[[label]], path)
      }
    }
    rm(d); gc()
  }
}


#8. Summarise 
# Per-fold Boyce, then mean and SD across folds for each model.
fold_table <- map_dfr(boyce_results, "folds")
fold_table

summary_table <- fold_table |>
  group_by(population, season, scenario) |>
  summarise(mean_boyce = mean(boyce),
            sd_boyce   = sd(boyce),
            min_boyce  = min(boyce),
            max_boyce  = max(boyce),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(tibble(label = names(boyce_results),
                   within_stratum_rho = map_dbl(boyce_results, "within_stratum_rho")) |>
              separate(label, c("population", "season", "scenario"), sep = " ", extra = "merge"),
            by = c("population", "season", "scenario"))
summary_table

#Frequency of used steps at each within-stratum rank (should climb toward the top rank)
map(boyce_results, "within_stratum_counts")
```

```{r}
set.seed(123)
rho_fixed <- map_dfr(boyce_results, function(r) {
  sc <- r$oof |>
    group_by(step_id_) |>
    filter(n() == 11) |>
    mutate(rank_in_stratum = rank(lp, ties.method = "random")) |>
    ungroup() |>
    filter(case_) |>
    count(rank_in_stratum, name = "n_used") |>
    complete(rank_in_stratum = 1:11, fill = list(n_used = 0))
  tibble(label = r$label,
         rho = cor(sc$rank_in_stratum, sc$n_used, method = "spearman"))
})
rho_fixed
```

```{r}
x <- boyce_results[["Etosha dry dist_only"]]$oof |>
  group_by(step_id_) |>
  summarise(n_unique = n_distinct(lp), .groups = "drop")

mean(x$n_unique == 1)   # share of strata where all 11 steps score identically
mean(x$n_unique < 11)   # share of strata with at least one tie
```

6.2e-05: only about 0.006% of strata have all 11 steps scoring identically. Almost every stratum has some variation for the model to use.
0.943: about 94% of strata have at least one tie among their 11 steps. Ties are everywhere, but mostly partial, such as two or three steps sharing a pixel.

```{r}
summary_table |>
  mutate(label = paste(population, season, scenario)) |>
  select(label, within_stratum_rho) |>
  left_join(rho_fixed, by = "label") |>
  rename(rho_first = within_stratum_rho, rho_random = rho)
```

The within-stratum result looks better than the Boyce result. That fits the idea that the SSF discriminates well within strata, while the pooled, cross-elephant Boyce is noisy because of variation between individuals.


#==============================================
#Boyce Cross-Validation for KAZA and Etosha
#==============================================
```{r}
#===============================
#Boyce Cross-Validation 
#===============================

# =============================================================================
# CONTINUOUS BOYCE INDEX VALIDATION FOR Etosha and KAZA (and Western when its model is updated)
# =============================================================================


#0. Packages
library(tidyverse)
library(survival)   # clogit()
library(modEvA)     # Boyce()
library(here)

set.seed(123)       # fold assignment is random


#0b. Settings
# NEW: choose which populations to run. West is switched off until its updated model/extraction exists
# (add "West" back here later; its old cached results in outputs/boyce are not touched).
# NEW: folder that holds the _v2.rds files
data_dir <- here("data", "ele_trk_data")
run_pops <- c("Etosha", "KAZA")   # any of "Etosha", "KAZA", "West"

# NEW: crossing terms with fewer used crossings than this in EITHER season are dropped for that
# population (a term with ~0 used crossings in a training fold gives a runaway coefficient).
# 50 = same rule as the v2 rerun in the SSF scripts (MIN_USED_CROSS).
min_used_cross <- 50


#1. Where the extracted step data live, and how to load them 
# NEW: Etosha and KAZA both come from the v2 extractions (new vet fences, vector-intersection crossings,
# new fence_dist). They are seasonal files, each already with a `season` column and step_id_ unique per elephant.
# The v2 files ALREADY contain fence_cross / road_cross / river_cross, so crossings are NOT rebuilt from
# the old *_linear columns (that would overwrite the new vector crossings).
# NEW: data are no longer all loaded up front. Each population is loaded inside the loop (section 7),
# trimmed to the columns needed, and dropped afterwards (KAZA + Etosha together is a lot of RAM).
# West must be rerun through extract_lc_mixed() so it has grassland/shrubland/tree_cover.
lin_cols <- c("kaza_vet_fences_linear", "roads_linear", "hydrorivers_linear")

# crossing indicators from the old 500 m *_linear columns; only used for West (not updated yet)
add_crossings <- function(d) {
  stopifnot(all(lin_cols %in% names(d)))
  d |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(
      across(all_of(lin_cols), ~ if_else(is.infinite(.x) | is.na(.x), 0, .x)),  # -Inf/NA = no feature
      fence_cross = as.integer(kaza_vet_fences_linear > 0),
      road_cross  = as.integer(roads_linear > 0),
      river_cross = as.integer(hydrorivers_linear > 0)
    )
}


#2. Choose covariates and settings
# NEW: base_vars = everything except core_dist; cross_vars = crossing indicators
base_vars  <- c("fence_dist", "road_dist", "water_rivers_dist",
                "cropland_dist", "grassland", "shrubland", "urban_dist",
                "tree_cover", "elevation", "slope", "aspect", "evi", "world_pop")
cross_vars <- c("fence_cross", "road_cross", "river_cross")

# NEW: load one population, keeping only the columns the models need (saves memory)
load_pop <- function(cfg) {
  keep <- unique(c("id", "step_id_", "case_", "season", base_vars, cross_vars, cfg$extra, lin_cols))
  d <- imap(cfg$paths, function(p, nm) {
    if (!file.exists(p)) stop("File not found: ", p, call. = FALSE)   # shows which path is wrong
    x <- readRDS(p) |> as_tibble() |> select(any_of(keep))
    if (!"season" %in% names(x)) x$season <- nm      # seasonal files: take season from the name
    x
  }) |> bind_rows()

  # NEW: make step_id_ unique across elephants (same rule as prep_season in the KAZA SSF script):
  # only prefix with the elephant id if it isn't already prefixed (Etosha v2 already is)
  prefixed <- all(startsWith(as.character(d$step_id_), paste0(d$id, "_")))
  if (!prefixed) d <- d |> mutate(step_id_ = paste(id, step_id_, sep = "_"))

  if (cfg$recompute_cross) d <- add_crossings(d) else stopifnot(all(cross_vars %in% names(d)))
  d |> select(-any_of(lin_cols))
}

#Etosha dropped core_dist because most Etosha steps are inside the core area.
# KAZA's SSF also has no core_dist, so only West adds it back via `extra`.
# NEW: the three linear-feature scenarios are built from base_vars. `cross_keep` = the crossing
# terms that have enough used crossings for this population (see min_used_cross above).
make_scenarios <- function(extra = character(0), cross_keep = cross_vars) {
  # each crossing term replaces its own distance-to term (river_cross has no pair)
  pairs    <- c(fence_cross = "fence_dist", road_cross = "road_dist")
  replaced <- unname(pairs[intersect(names(pairs), cross_keep)])
  scn <- list(
    dist_only       = c(extra, base_vars),                                   # 1. distance-to only
    dist_plus_cross = c(extra, base_vars, cross_keep),                       # 2. distance-to + crossings
    cross_only      = c(extra, setdiff(base_vars, replaced), cross_keep)     # 3. crossings replace fence/road distance
  )
  scn[!duplicated(map(scn, sort))]     # if no crossing terms survive, drop the duplicate scenarios
}

# NEW: per-population settings. recompute_cross: TRUE = build crossings from the *_linear columns;
# FALSE = the file already has them (v2 files).
pops <- list(
  Etosha = list(paths = c(wet = file.path(data_dir, "ele_trk_extract_etosha_wet_v2.rds"),
                          dry = file.path(data_dir, "ele_trk_extract_etosha_dry_v2.rds")),
                extra = character(0), fill_lc_na = TRUE, recompute_cross = FALSE),
  KAZA   = list(paths = c(wet = file.path(data_dir, "ele_trk_extract_kaza_wet_v2.rds"),
                          dry = file.path(data_dir, "ele_trk_extract_kaza_dry_v2.rds")),
                extra = character(0), fill_lc_na = TRUE, recompute_cross = FALSE),
  West   = list(paths = c(all = here("outputs", "ele_trk_extract_west.rds")),
                extra = "core_dist",  fill_lc_na = FALSE, recompute_cross = TRUE)
)[run_pops]

k_folds <- 5     #number of CV folds (capped at the number of elephants)
bin_width <- 0.1   #moving-window width, in units of the prediction scale
n_windows <- 100   #number of window positions along the gradient (modEvA `res`)
pred_scale <- "rank"  # "rank" or "lp" -- see section 5 for the decision
n_per_stratum <- 11   # 1 used + 10 random steps

boyce_dir <- here("outputs", "boyce")   # NEW: per-model cache folder
dir.create(boyce_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)


#3.Prepare a season-specific dataset 
prep_data <- function(trk, season_label, vars, fill_lc_na = FALSE) {

  stopifnot(all(vars %in% names(trk)))   # NEW: fails loudly if columns are missing (e.g. West without lcmixed)

  d <- trk |>
    as_tibble() |>                       # drop the amt track class; plain tibble is safer
    filter(season == season_label)

  # NEW: step_id_ must be unique across elephants, or whole-elephant folds would split strata
  stopifnot(nrow(distinct(d, step_id_, id)) == n_distinct(d$step_id_))

  # In Etosha pipeline set missing binary land cover to 0 (pixels outside the land-cover raster). Keep that here.
  if (fill_lc_na) {
    d <- d |> mutate(across(c(grassland, shrubland, tree_cover), ~ replace_na(.x, 0)))
  }

  d |>
    #The same complete rows must be used to fit and to score, so drop NAs in any model covariate up front.
    # NEW: `vars` is the union across all scenarios so every scenario uses identical rows.
    drop_na(all_of(vars)) |>
    # Dropping rows can orphan a stratum (case removed but controls kept, or
    # vice versa). A stratum needs >= 1 case and >= 1 control to be informative.
    group_by(step_id_) |>
    filter(any(case_), any(!case_)) |>
    ungroup()
}


#4.Assign whole elephants to folds
# NEW: now called once per population x season (outside run_ssf_boyce) so all scenarios share folds
make_folds <- function(data, k) {
  ids <- unique(data$id)
  k   <- min(k, length(ids))             #can't have more folds than animals
  fold_tbl <- tibble(id = sample(ids),   #shuffle animals, then deal into folds
                     fold = rep_len(seq_len(k), length(ids)))
  left_join(data, fold_tbl, by = "id")
}


#Fit the SSF and score new steps
fit_ssf <- function(train, vars) {
  f <- reformulate(c(vars, "strata(step_id_)"), response = "case_")
  # With one used step per stratum, method = "efron" gives the same estimates
  # as clogit's default "exact", but is much faster on millions of rows.
  clogit(f, data = train, method = "efron")
}

# Linear predictor for new data: X %*% beta (log relative selection strength).
score_steps <- function(fit, newdata) {
  b <- coef(fit)
  b <- b[!is.na(b)]
  X <- as.matrix(newdata[, names(b)])
  drop(X %*% b)
}


#6.Cross-validated Boyce for one model
# NEW: `data` already has a fold column; `meta` carries population/season/scenario labels
run_ssf_boyce <- function(data, vars, label, meta) {

  folds <- sort(unique(data$fold))
  oof   <- list()   #out-of-fold predictions, kept for the pooled plot
  res   <- list()   #one row of summary stats per fold

  for (f in folds) {
    message(label, ": fold ", f, " of ", length(folds))

    train <- filter(data, fold != f)
    test  <- filter(data, fold == f)

    fit <- fit_ssf(train, vars)
    test$lp <- score_steps(fit, test)      # log-RSS of every held-out step


    #Scale is "rank": Converts the linear predictor into a uniform percentile rank from 0 to 1. Every window gets a roughly equal number of data points, making the P/E ratio stable across the gradient. Boyce is rank-based anyway (Spearman).
    test$pred <- if (pred_scale == "rank") percent_rank(test$lp) else test$lp

    #`obs` must be numeric 0/1 (1 = used step, 0 = random step).
    #modEvA compares predictions at used steps against predictions across
    #ALL steps, i.e. presence vs "available".
    b <- Boyce(obs = as.numeric(test$case_),
               pred = test$pred,
               n.bins = NA,                # NA = continuous moving window
               bin.width = if (pred_scale == "rank") bin_width else "default",
               res = n_windows,
               method = "spearman",
               rm.dup.classes = FALSE,
               plot = FALSE)

    res[[f]] <- tibble(
      meta,                                # NEW: population / season / scenario
      label = label, fold = f,
      n_elephants = n_distinct(test$id),
      n_used_steps = sum(test$case_),
      boyce = b$B,
      #modEvA flags windows with < 30 points (their P/E ratio is noisy)
      n_small_bins = sum(b$bins$bin.N < 30, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
    oof[[f]] <- test |> select(step_id_, case_, lp, pred, fold)
    rm(train, test, fit); gc()             # NEW: free memory between folds
  }

  oof <- bind_rows(oof)

  #Pooled out-of-fold P/E curve
  # A good model gives a monotonically increasing curve. Pooling predictions across folds gives one curve per model.
  Boyce(obs = as.numeric(oof$case_), pred = oof$pred,
        bin.width = if (pred_scale == "rank") bin_width else "default",
        res = n_windows, plot = TRUE,
        main = paste("Boyce (out-of-fold):", label))

  #Check: within-stratum rank of the used step 
  # Because an SSF compares each used step to ITS OWN random steps, also ask:
  # where does the used step rank among the steps in its stratum?
  # (Fortin et al. 2009-style). If the model works, used steps should land at
  # the high ranks far more often than the 1/n expected by chance.
  # NEW: uncommented, and n_per_stratum replaces the max(table(...)) lookup (slow on millions of rows);
  # complete() fills ranks with zero counts so the correlation is always over 1:11
  strata_check <- oof |>
    group_by(step_id_) |>
    filter(n() == n_per_stratum) |>                # keep complete strata (e.g. 11 steps)
    mutate(rank_in_stratum = rank(lp, ties.method = "random")) |>  #method for ranking steps. So when there are steps of identical score, this tie is shuffles them so that they are equally likely to land at any position in it rather than "first" which ranks whichever step comes first which is always the used which gets ranked lowest everytime then.  
    ungroup() |>
    filter(case_) |>
    count(rank_in_stratum, name = "n_used") |>
    complete(rank_in_stratum = 1:n_per_stratum, fill = list(n_used = 0))

  within_stratum_rho <- cor(strata_check$rank_in_stratum, strata_check$n_used,
                            method = "spearman")

  list(label = label,
       folds = bind_rows(res),
       oof = oof,
       within_stratum_counts = strata_check,
       within_stratum_rho = within_stratum_rho)
}


#7. Run for each population x season 
# NEW: also x scenario; each result is cached so reruns skip finished models
# NEW: each population is loaded here, then released before the next one.
# NOTE: cached results are reused by name (e.g. "KAZA_wet_dist_only.rds"). If you change the crossing
# terms, input files, or covariates, delete the matching files in outputs/boyce so they are refit.
boyce_results <- list()

for (pop in names(pops)) {
  cfg <- pops[[pop]]
  message("Loading ", pop, " ...")
  pop_dat <- load_pop(cfg)

  # NEW: which crossing terms have enough USED crossings (in both seasons) to be estimated?
  used_cross <- pop_dat |>
    filter(case_) |>
    group_by(season) |>
    summarise(across(all_of(cross_vars), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), n_used = n(), .groups = "drop")
  print(used_cross)
  cross_keep <- cross_vars[map_lgl(cross_vars, ~ min(used_cross[[.x]]) >= min_used_cross)]
  if (length(setdiff(cross_vars, cross_keep)))
    message(pop, ": dropping crossing terms with < ", min_used_cross, " used crossings: ",
            paste(setdiff(cross_vars, cross_keep), collapse = ", "))

  scn      <- make_scenarios(cfg$extra, cross_keep)
  all_vars <- unique(unlist(scn))

  for (szn in c("wet", "dry")) {
    d <- prep_data(pop_dat, szn, all_vars, fill_lc_na = cfg$fill_lc_na)

    set.seed(123)                      # NEW: same fold assignment for every scenario
    d <- make_folds(d, k_folds)

    for (sc in names(scn)) {
      label <- paste(pop, szn, sc)
      path  <- file.path(boyce_dir, paste0(gsub(" ", "_", label), ".rds"))

      if (file.exists(path)) {
        boyce_results[[label]] <- readRDS(path)
      } else {
        meta <- tibble(population = pop, season = szn, scenario = sc)
        boyce_results[[label]] <- run_ssf_boyce(d, scn[[sc]], label, meta)
        saveRDS(boyce_results[[label]], path)
      }
    }
    rm(d); gc()
  }
  rm(pop_dat); gc()
}


#8. Summarise 
# Per-fold Boyce, then mean and SD across folds for each model.
fold_table <- map_dfr(boyce_results, "folds")
fold_table

summary_table <- fold_table |>
  group_by(population, season, scenario) |>
  summarise(mean_boyce = mean(boyce),
            sd_boyce   = sd(boyce),
            min_boyce  = min(boyce),
            max_boyce  = max(boyce),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(tibble(label = names(boyce_results),
                   within_stratum_rho = map_dbl(boyce_results, "within_stratum_rho")) |>
              separate(label, c("population", "season", "scenario"), sep = " ", extra = "merge"),
            by = c("population", "season", "scenario"))
summary_table

#Frequency of used steps at each within-stratum rank (should climb toward the top rank)
map(boyce_results, "within_stratum_counts")


# Column check (data are no longer kept in memory after the loop, so this loads each population).
# Every covariate the models expect but the data lacks (should be character(0) for each):
if (FALSE) {
  for (pop in names(pops)) {
    d <- load_pop(pops[[pop]])
    cat(pop, "- missing:", setdiff(unique(unlist(make_scenarios(pops[[pop]]$extra))), names(d)), "\n")
    rm(d); gc()
  }
}
```

```{r}
set.seed(123)
rho_fixed <- map_dfr(boyce_results, function(r) {
  sc <- r$oof |>
    group_by(step_id_) |>
    filter(n() == 11) |>
    mutate(rank_in_stratum = rank(lp, ties.method = "random")) |>
    ungroup() |>
    filter(case_) |>
    count(rank_in_stratum, name = "n_used") |>
    complete(rank_in_stratum = 1:11, fill = list(n_used = 0))
  tibble(label = r$label,
         rho = cor(sc$rank_in_stratum, sc$n_used, method = "spearman"))
})
rho_fixed
```

```{r}
# NEW: tie check now runs for every population/season (dist_only model), not just Etosha dry
tie_check <- map_dfr(names(boyce_results)[str_detect(names(boyce_results), "dist_only$")], function(l) {
  x <- boyce_results[[l]]$oof |>
    group_by(step_id_) |>
    summarise(n_unique = n_distinct(lp), .groups = "drop")
  tibble(label = l,
         share_all_identical = mean(x$n_unique == 1),   # share of strata where all 11 steps score identically
         share_any_tie       = mean(x$n_unique < 11))   # share of strata with at least one tie
})
tie_check

# Etosha dry result from before:
# 6.2e-05: only about 0.006% of strata have all 11 steps scoring identically. Almost every stratum has some variation for the model to use.
# 0.943: about 94% of strata have at least one tie among their 11 steps. Ties are everywhere, but mostly partial, such as two or three steps sharing a pixel.
```

```{r}

summary_table |>
  mutate(label = paste(population, season, scenario)) |>
  select(label, within_stratum_rho) |>
  left_join(rho_fixed, by = "label") |>
  rename(rho_first = within_stratum_rho, rho_random = rho)
```
